story: On Magnolia Loop at 9:17 on a mild, partly cloudy Wednesday night, Gary is walking Hal through a portable speaker setup he's clipped to a golf cart roof rail, explaining that sound has to cut off at ten under the community rules. Donna, cheerful and clearly scheming, invites Gary to her place tomorrow morning to learn paddleball and claim a spot on the ladder, while Rosa, content as ever, promises to make room for her dessert. Hal, dutifully counting the flamingos in Donna's yard, is set to log eleven in his notebook, and Rosa suspects he'll want a recount.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street myself and jot the tally in my notebook

gary.thought_process: Hal asked to see the form and how the lights and speakers are mounted, and I already handed it over last tick. Now he's waiting on my details, so I shouldn't repeat myself. Give him the specifics: LED strip on the roof rail, speakers under the rear seat, nothing sticking out past the cart body, and the 10 PM cutoff is in writing per L-03. L-01 says exterior mods visible from the street need Architectural Review, so doing it by the book keeps the parade plan clean. Getting this done with Hal means I can relax and focus on the cornbread for Friday.

parameters.content: Strip's clipped along the roof rail with no drilling, and the speakers sit under the rear seat, so nothing sticks out past the body. Sound cuts at ten sharp, per L-03, and it's written in the margin for you.

donna.thought_process: It's 9:17 PM on Wednesday and Gary is right here, deep in cart-form paperwork with Hal. Rosa already confirmed Friday at six and I've answered her, so no need to repeat that. My real goal is getting Gary a paddle and onto the ladder, and Tuesday's lesson is on my mind. Hal's handling the form, so I shouldn't crowd that. A short, forward-moving nudge to Gary about paddle shopping tomorrow keeps my recruiting plan moving without repeating myself.

parameters.content: Gary, once Hal's got your form squared away, come by my place tomorrow morning and I'll walk you through picking out a paddle. The ladder won't climb itself, and I've already got us a spot on the board.

hal.thought_process: Gary already handed me the form and told me the details: LED strip on the roof rail, speakers under the rear seat, ten o'clock cutoff in writing. Donna says eleven flamingos, which is eight over the L-02 limit of three visible from the street. I said I'd keep my own tally honest, so I'll check the flock myself and look at the actual count from the street, not take anyone's word for it. Rosa's Friday dinner stays out of the rulebook, though. Tonight it's by the book, and the form comes first.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street myself and jot the tally in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: It's 9:17 PM and everyone's confirmed for Friday at six: Donna with dessert, Gary with cornbread, Hal helping Gary finish the form. I already invited them last tick, so asking again would be nagging. Donna just spoke to me, though, and she deserves a reply, and I can tease her about the flamingos. Quiet hours start at ten, so a short, warm word to Donna and then I head home to set the table fits.

parameters.content: Dessert is welcome, Donna, I'll find the room. And eleven flamingos, all within the law? Hal's going to want a recount.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
